verdict.rationale: Crossmint lets a user grant an agent its own signer key bound to a permission set the user signs off on: spend cap, allowed counterparties and time window. These limits are enforced onchain and revocable at any time. Agent cards add a second kind of scoped credential: one-time card credentials tied to a fixed allowance, expiry and locked merchant, while the agent never sees the real card number. Missing for 10: no evidence that Crossmint's own platform API keys can be scoped per agent (client-side keys only document URL whitelisting), and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the delegation model.
